examples: Ask an agent in one pane what other sessions are running and what state they are in, without leaving its prompt.
An agent asks to stop a runaway session, you see the request, and approve it.
An agent on one computer lists the paired computer's sessions, reads one, and asks to restart it; the request waits in your inbox.
Ask one agent to send a task to another; it waits safely if the receiver is busy or in a dialog.
An agent calls agents_lookup with view roster and scope around, reads each session's short description and its project and company, and skips the archived ones.
how_to: Start or restart a claude or codex session: it registers a server named carnivore by itself, ready for the first turn.
Ask an agent to use the carnivore tools. For another agent, run agents_lookup and crosstalk_send; the first contact asks for owner approval.

The hold is off by default. With it on, an agent's keys, restart or stop aimed at another session wait for your approval (GET /api/v1/agent-actions, then POST /api/v1/agent-actions/{id}/approve or /deny). Turn that hold on or off with PUT /api/v1/agent-actions/settings {"gate_cross_session_actions": true}. The server itself is on by default; switching it off in settings lists every feature that stops working first.
To turn the server off, set mcp.enabled to false in config.json and restart the session.

Before messaging another session, ask an agent to call agents_lookup with view roster: scope online (live), around (live and asleep) or all (archived included, marked archived: true); has_description finds sessions with or without a short or long description.
media_exempt: no interface of its own: the agent's own prompt shows the tools, and the proof is a scripted test against the real claude and codex binaries
name: Carnivore MCP server
summary: claude and codex sessions use carnivore tools to inspect sessions, act with owner approval, and exchange durable crosstalk messages.
where: Inside any claude or codex pane: the agent lists a server named carnivore.
